doc.title: Billie Pierce and De De Pierce Interview, 1959-10-07

title: Decatur Street night spots
summary: They list the clubs on Decatur Street where they worked, including Popeye's, the Kingfish and a Filipino place.

story.theme_name: Gangsters, bootleggers and rough clubs of Prohibition
story.community_name: Cabarets, honky-tonks and the Storyville nightlife scene

blocks.x: Speaking Spanish comes in handy. Yeah. It was what helped Alvarez too when he was on the wrong spot speaking Spanish, you know. Let's see, we had you down on Decatur Street there and you all got married. Where did you play before you played at the Kingfish, was that it?
No.
Well, when I got married to Didi.
Mm-hmm.

Well, I was working at the Kingfish when I met you. Yeah. When I met you. And before that? Well, I was at the Rialto nightclub. And I wait for... When did Popeye's come in? Well, I worked at Popeye right there on Decatur Street. We worked there together. We worked at Popeye right there on Decatur Street. Left West Line Decatur.
West Line Decatur.
All right next door, next door like that.
I went on the spot on Decatur. All right. Leave one and go in there.
Leave one and go in there.
Get in a little, you know, based on the sand, we crossed the street and go in the next block. That's what we did. Mm-hmm. Every one of those spots at that time. What were those spots down there?
The dog. They had the... Cat in the Fizzle, one.
No, not down on Decatur Street.
They had Popeye. They had the Kingfish.
Kingfish.
They had Charlie Palooka. That's why you were getting Charlie Palooka with Sadie. And they had... The Mars place. Corrine. Corrine. And further on down, they had Spanish place, you know.
Yeah, I worked there.

Filipinas, what I mean. Filipinas, I worked there. Filipinas in there. They had nightclubs too, all right around in there. There's so many. Right around the gallery, just like that. You walk out of the door right in there. All around there. Hold a minute. Hold a minute. Hold a minute. Hold a minute. Hold a minute. Hold a minute. Hold a minute. Hold a minute.

Hold a minute. over there was a Filipino place over there, and right across over there on the next corner there was Big Landry and them played with the Lady in Red, and Kid Howard, all of them was out there, Jim Crow, the Army, all the color bands, you know that town was right around Decatur Street, right around that section.
We would just switch around from job to job, that's what we did.
